original_question: Let P be a univariate polynomial of degree d >= 2, and for integers n >= 1 and 0 <= m <= nd define Q_{n,m}(x) = d^m(P(x)^n)/dx^m. Let Upsilon_P be the closure of the union of all roots of all Q_{n,m}(x). If the roots of P are in convex position but do not form a regular polygon, must Upsilon_P be a closed domain inside the convex hull of the roots of P, with all critical points of P on the boundary of Upsilon_P, no inflection points on that boundary, and boundary contained in the union of the critical values, with respect to z, of F_alpha(z) = z - alpha P(z)/P'(z) as alpha ranges over [0,d]?
target_in_paper: Boris Shapiro, §1 "On shadows of polynomials": the paragraph defining the shadow Υ_P, followed by Conjecture 1 and the immediately following Remark 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target very closely: it introduces the descendants Q_{n,m}, defines the shadow Υ_P as the closure of the union of their roots, uses the convex-position/non-regular-polygon hypothesis, and asks for exactly the four geometric properties stated in Conjecture 1, including the description via the critical values of F_α(z)=z-αP(z)/P'(z). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
missing_details: The paper is working in the complex plane, so a stand-alone formulation should say explicitly that P is a complex univariate polynomial P(z) and that the closure is taken in C. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
It is cleaner to use the paper’s variable z rather than x, since the conjecture later speaks about critical values with respect to z. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

For full stand-alone clarity, the geometric hypothesis should specify what "roots are in convex position" means, since this section uses the phrase but does not unpack it locally. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
A paper-faithful restatement should present the claim as four explicit clauses (i)–(iv), mirroring Conjecture 1, rather than as one long sentence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The notions of "critical points of P" and "critical values of F_α" should be made explicit in a stand-alone question: the former are zeros of P'(z), and the latter are critical values of the rational function F_α in the variable z. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The nearby context includes Remark 1, which records an equivalent reformulation of one clause of the conjecture; your draft does not mention that nearby paper-supplied reformulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
refined_question: Let P(z)∈C[z] be a univariate polynomial of degree d≥2. For integers n≥1 and 0≤m≤nd, define Q_{n,m}(z):=d^m/dz^m(P(z)^n), and let Υ_P⊂C be the closure of the union of the zero sets of all Q_{n,m}. If the roots of P are in convex position, but do not form a regular polygon, is it true that: (i) Υ_P is a closed domain contained in the convex hull of the roots of P; (ii) every critical point of P lies on ∂Υ_P; (iii) ∂Υ_P has no inflection points; and (iv) ∂Υ_P is contained in the union, over α∈[0,d], of the critical values with respect to z of the rational function F_α(z)=z-αP(z)/P'(z)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
justification: The draft is aiming at Boris Shapiro’s open problem in the subsection "On shadows of polynomials," not at a broader neighboring topic. The section first defines the double-indexed family Q_{n,m} and the shadow Υ_P as the closure of the union of their roots, then states Conjecture 1 with exactly the four properties listed in your draft, and finally adds a nearby Remark 1 with an equivalent reformulation of one part of the conjecture. The main sharpening needed is therefore not to broaden the mathematics, but only to make the ambient setting C, the role of the variable z, and the clause-by-clause structure explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
